{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=computational+models+of+episodic+memory+and+preference+formation+in+autonomous+agents&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.31224/5919\", \"title\": [\"Active Dreaming Memory: Biologically-Inspired Episodic Consolidation for Lifelong Learning in Autonomous Agents\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Autonomous agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) often suffer from catastrophic forgetting and lack temporal continuity. We present Active Dreaming Memory (ADM), a biologically-inspired dual-store memory system that enables agents to learn from execution failures without fine-tuning. Our key innovation is a counterfactual verification mechanism that validates candidate rules through synthetic scenario simulation before committing them to long-term memory. Experiments across six diverse domains demonstrate that ADM improves first-episode learning efficiency by 2× and achieves 83% success rate, significantly outperforming Reflexion, MemGPT, and Self-RAG. Catastrophic forgetting stress tests show 95% retention after 500 episodes. Theoretical analysis proves bounded forgetting guarantees and logarithmic memory growth. We release open-source code to support reproducible lifelong learning research.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.31224/5919\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 12, 3]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7286873\", \"title\": [\"Dual Memory System: A Method for Affective-Weighted Episodic–Semantic Memory Consolidation for Continual Learning in Autonomous Agents\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Autonomous agents operating over long horizons must retain specific experiences, generalize recurring structure, and decide which memories are worth keeping, without collapsing into an undifferentiated buffer that grows without bound or loses interpretability. We present a method for building such a system, the Dual Memory System (DMS), modeled on the brain&apos;s separation between a fast hippocampal episodic store and a slow neocortical semantic store, with an affective-weighting mechanism inspired by amygdala-gated consolidation. The method specifies how to encode experiences into dense embeddings and affect labels, rank them for rehearsal using an interpretable, decomposable importance function, cluster and abstract high-rehearsal memories into semantic records under an explicit faithfulness check, and decay low-importance records over time. Unlike the black-box relevance scores used in comparable agent-memory systems, every step of the DMS pipeline is logged and independently inspectable.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7286873\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1109/hsi.2008.4581512\", \"title\": [\"Episodic memory for autonomous agents\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/hsi.2008.4581512\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2008, 5]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1017/9781108755610.022\", \"title\": [\"Computational Models of Episodic Memory\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1017/9781108755610.022\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2023, 5, 11]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "5b8bf76a8d7b1180245039c9eb746e1c900e8d925aeb98fa05c17e77feb3841c", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "memory_formed_preferences", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.31224/5919", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7286873", "doi:10.1109/hsi.2008.4581512", "doi:10.1017/9781108755610.022"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.31224/5919", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7286873", "https://doi.org/10.1109/hsi.2008.4581512", "https://doi.org/10.1017/9781108755610.022"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
